strategyOwner: Violet Adams / GTMx outbound (Richard Haigh thread)
headline: Your IntelliEvent waterfall journey.
subheadline: A scrollable GTMx strategy artifact for routing event rental, AV, party, tent, and production companies into the right IntelliEvent Lightning switch, comparison, or ops-playbook offer. List building, campaign angles, and sample copy, prepared for Richard Haigh, Director, European Business Development.
productSummary: IntelliEvent Lightning (intellievent.com; Extreme Impact / extreme-impact.com) is cloud-based event rental and labor management software for rental companies, venues, and AV / production pros. Homepage positioning: manage the entire workflow — sales & quoting, inventory control, warehouse management, logistics & operations, accounting & reports, and labor scheduling — anytime, anywhere, any device. Published modules and add-ons include availability calendar, RFID / barcode check-in-out, multi-location warehouse, truck routing & dispatch, Global Labor Scheduler + mobile labor app, IntelliSign, IntelliTime, Advanced CRM, Survey, Vendor Catalog, Assembly, and accounting hand-off. Integrations named on site: QuickBooks, Google Calendar, Avalara. Site claim: more than 1,000 customers spanning AV, lighting, staging, party, tent, and special effects worldwide; transforming rental ops since 1997. Named customer proof on site: Expert'ease, Crescent Event Productions, AVT Productions, AVFX, Nationwide, On Services. Richard Haigh is Director, European Business Development (rhaigh@extreme-impact.com).
coreInsight: Richard sells one IntelliEvent Lightning platform — quote-to-invoice rental ops + warehouse + logistics + labor — not a different product per niche. Party vs AV vs tent vs venue is a merge tag after routing, not a second waterfall. The single routing signal is competitor_rental_os: which event/AV rental management stack a lead source can already see (Rentman / Current RMS–OnRent Events, other cloud rental OS, spreadsheet / QuickBooks-centric ops without a rental OS, or none). That ladder maps to Lightning's live offers: competitor switch + migration, feature/ops comparison, spreadsheet-to-Lightning ops brief, then a soft remaining-TAM Lightning playbook.

sections.title: The signal is which rental OS they already run
sections.takeaway: BuiltWith, careers, job ads, and partner/tech mentions already show Rentman, Current RMS / OnRent Events, Booqable, Goodshuffle Pro, Point of Rental, or spreadsheet / QuickBooks-only ops. That competitor_rental_os is stronger than a title guess and cheap to collect.

sections.label: Waterfall
sections.title: One cascade routes every in-TAM event rental and AV account
sections.takeaway: First match wins. Rentman / Current RMS first, then other cloud rental OS, then spreadsheet / QuickBooks-centric ops, then every remaining party, tent, AV, and production rental company.

sections.label: Launch
sections.title: Launch the Rentman / Current RMS switch route first
sections.takeaway: Start where competitor_rental_os already shows Rentman or Current RMS / OnRent Events. Prove reply density, then roll other-OS comparison, spreadsheet-to-Lightning, and the remaining-TAM catch-all.

signalReasons: Apollo / LinkedIn Sales Nav (event rental, party rental, AV hire, production rental, tent & structure, lighting, staging, venue AV) plus industry directories (ARA member lists, Eventective / wedding-vendor rental categories, local chamber rental categories) are the TAM IntelliEvent already sells into. Exact public TAM account count is not published on intellievent.com; treat size as estimated (see intellievent-magnet-flags.txt) and keep each launch tier >=~1,500 contacts where possible.

The same BuiltWith + careers + job-ad scrape returns competitor_rental_os: Rentman / Current RMS (OnRent Events); other cloud rental OS (Booqable, Goodshuffle Pro, Point of Rental, EZRentOut, HireTrack, MCS, RigER, EventBound, Stagera, RentalHQ, adjacent); spreadsheet / QuickBooks-centric ops (job ads naming Excel inventory, Google Sheets dispatch, QuickBooks as primary ops without a rental OS brand); or none — enough to route without a second expensive enrichment product.

The ladder maps to live IntelliEvent Lightning positioning (sales & quoting, inventory & warehouse, logistics & routing, labor scheduling + mobile, QuickBooks / Google Calendar / Avalara integrations, 250+ reports) plus public proof language (1,000+ customers; Expert'ease, Crescent Event Productions, AVT Productions, AVFX, Nationwide, On Services).

Segment (party vs AV vs tent vs lighting vs venue vs staging) and region (US / UK / EU / ROW) are scrape filters and merge tags, not a second waterfall. Apollo is email last after the account is routed.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND competitor_rental_os_family = rentman_current (Rentman, Current RMS, OnRent Events / OnRent) AND not already_customer
routingRules.then: Tier 1 - Rentman / Current RMS Switch + Migration Brief
routingRules.why: They already pay for the dominant AV / production rental OS. Strongest switch intent for IntelliEvent Lightning quote-to-invoice + warehouse + labor with a migration magnet.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND competitor_rental_os_family = other_cloud_rental_os (Booqable, Goodshuffle Pro, Point of Rental, EZRentOut, HireTrack, MCS, RigER, EventBound, Stagera, RentalHQ, adjacent) AND not already_customer
routingRules.why: They run a competing cloud rental OS. Side-by-side Lightning pitch on inventory forecasting, multi-warehouse, logistics routing, and labor scheduling vs their current tool.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND competitor_rental_os_family = spreadsheet_qb_ops (job ads / site language shows Excel / Google Sheets / Access inventory or QuickBooks-as-primary ops without a rental OS brand) AND not already_customer
routingRules.why: Visible spreadsheet / QB ops without a rental OS. Maps to Lightning inventory + warehouse + labor replacing manual shortage and crew chaos.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND none of the above
routingRules.why: Still in TAM (event rental / AV / party / tent / staging / venue operators). Softest CTA around quote-to-invoice clarity, inventory accuracy, and labor visibility. Mandatory 100% coverage.
